alt: A driver mutation gives a clone in tissue that is still working; further drivers over decades, together with controls giving way, give growth that does not end.
longDescription: A driver mutation contributes a growth advantage and gives a clone within working tissue. That the tissue is still working is an observation from the normal-skin study, which measured mutation and clonal selection and found gross tissue function preserved; which particular controls were holding, and whether they are what kept the clone benign, that study did not measure and this map does not claim. Over decades the clone may acquire further drivers, a typical tumour carrying two to eight, and growth that does not end follows from those accumulated drivers together with the giving way of the tissue's own controls. Other context matters and is not drawn here: immune surveillance, the surrounding stroma, which lineage the cell belongs to, and which particular variant it carries. The map's point is that one driver is not sufficient, and that what happens next depends on the tissue as well as on the mutation.
